Walmart announces it will officially support Apple Pay starting next week. After resisting pressure from consumers to offer Apple Pay support for over a decade, the retailer has finally decided to give in.

Apple Pay finally arrives at Walmart

Walmart announced the news in a press release today. Starting August 24, the company will begin rolling out contactless payment support, including Apple Pay, at select Walmart and Sam's Club locations. Full nationwide coverage across all stores is expected by the end of this year, with expansion to fuel stations by mid-2027.

Walmart will add broad contactless payment support, covering Apple Pay and Google Pay on iPhone and Apple Watch, contactless credit cards, and other payment platforms. Customers will also be able to add Walmart and Sam's Club membership cards to platforms like Apple Wallet. The new support will operate alongside existing payment methods, including Walmart Pay.

The company stated:

Walmart is one of the last major retailers still not supporting Apple Pay, making this big news for consumers. For years, the retailer has refused to offer contactless payments, instead pushing its own QR code-based payment system, Walmart Pay.

As recently as last year, Walmart still firmly believed Walmart Pay was more convenient for consumers than Apple Pay. However, to use Walmart Pay, users must first link a credit or debit card within the Walmart app on iPhone, then scan a QR code at checkout to complete payment with their iPhone.

A quick search on social media reveals just how frustrated users have been with Walmart's refusal to support Apple Pay.

After all, other retailers that long refused Apple Pay support have caved in over the years, including Kroger, Home Depot, and H-E-B—and for good reason.

Does Walmart's lack of Apple Pay support affect your shopping habits? Once they roll out Apple Pay, will you be more inclined to shop at Walmart and Sam's Club? Let us know in the comments.
